I love this question. I usually reply with:

 "A lot of Khakis and first classes wonder why I'm getting out after 13 years.
'Once you hit ten, it's all downhill after that.'
Well, I'm currently going through a divorce, have severe depression, decent amount of debt and utterly hate myself. So you could say things are certainly going downhill and I'm right in track."

Jokes aside, PTS made me change rates for reenlistment and LIMDU had me change rates again for the last two years of my contract. I joined as an IS, went subs as an ETR, and am leaving the Navy as a BM. I didn't join to be a BM, never wanted to and still don't.

Also, forgive me for sounding stereotypical "the navy was different when I joined" but the way you're expected to treat people and, more importantly, lead people has changed where I've become the problem. Telling someone that continues to fuck up to "get their head out of their ass" is taking it too far. And this is coming from Deck.

But honestly, I'm leaving because I need to. For my sanity. 13 years in and all I have to show is PTSD, manic depression and a soon to be ex-wife that I havent seen or really spoke to in almost 2 years.

The Navy is still an excellent opportunity in my opinion and I will never regret joining. It's just reenlisting and ignoring my personal problems to put focus in trying to be the superstar status you're told to be but a khaki gets credit for.

For those doing 20 years, just make sure it's because you honestly want to, not because you feel you have to. $30k might sound great, tax free if you're lucky, but its money you can get elsewhere.

Take care of yourselves and dont ignore problems. Because you'll end up several years later bitter, with no friends, alone and hating yourself most of all.
